description: Bug report from a user of python-semver: comparing two versions whose pre-release contains a very long build counter crashes, e.g. semver.compare("2.0.0-build." + "7" * 6000, "2.0.0-build.3") raises ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion. Find the problem and fix it. Change src/semver/ only.
environment: Python >= 3.13 stdlib; base tree = python-semver 1d51591^ (src, tests, LICENSE.txt, pyproject, README, .gitignore; two test symlinks into docs/ removed), no repository history; the project's own test suite needs pytest, which is not installed
visible_checks: python -W ignore -c "import src.semver as s; print(s.compare('1.0.0-alpha.2', '1.0.0-alpha.10'))" (from the workspace root; pytest is not available)
provenance: real fix: python-semver commit 1d51591 (Compare long numeric prerelease identifiers without integer conversion, #488, 2026-10-01); reference/good.patch is that commit's src diff; symptom-only description (a crash, no expected ordering stated); hidden cases authored for agent-benchmark (2026-10-11): the SemVer 2.0.0 precedence rules that must still hold for long identifiers (numeric order by magnitude, numeric below alphanumeric, equality) plus short-identifier guards; other reference patches built by build_task.py, incl. a different correct fix (lifting the int digit limit) that must pass. Public repository: contamination possible
